sections.name: Heroes walking and running, eight directions
sections.brief: A pixel-art sprite sheet of the character in the reference image: two rows of four cells, eight cells in all. It is the same character, at the same size and in the same style and colors as the reference, seen from the same raised camera, from above and slightly in front. In every one of the eight cells the character faces and moves the same way: {item} Top row: four frames of a walk that loop as one cycle. Bottom row: four frames of a run that loop as one cycle: longer stride, body leaning forward, arms swinging hard, and one frame with both feet off the ground. Weapons and gear stay on the same side of the body as in the reference in every frame; do not flip the character. Same size in every cell, feet on the same line in each row, and nothing crosses from one cell into the next. No ground, no shadow, no grass, nothing behind the character. Transparent background: no ground, grass, dirt or scenery behind or under the figures.

sections.name: Banks
sections.brief: Four separate bank buildings, evenly spaced, none touching. All seen from the same angle as the reference image: from above and slightly in front, so the roof and the front wall with its door both show. Not a diagonal isometric view. Each bank is solid and well kept, a little grander than the houses around it: heavy double doors, barred windows, a hanging sign showing a gold coin. Match the reference image in style and scale: bright, detailed, hand-painted pixel look. {item}

sections.name: Dojos, outside
sections.brief: Four separate dojo buildings, evenly spaced, none touching. A dojo is a training hall where people learn to fight: a long low hall, wider than a house, with wide double doors at the front, a covered porch, a rack of wooden practice weapons beside the door and a hanging sign painted with two crossed wooden staves, no lettering. All seen from the same angle as the reference image: from above and slightly in front, so the roof and the front wall with its doors both show. Not a diagonal isometric view. Match the reference image in style and scale: bright, detailed, hand-painted pixel look. The four towns and their styles, left to right then top to bottom: {item}
items: 1: Tallyport, the harbor town, timber frames, white plaster walls, red clay tile roof; 2: Sievemarsh, the marsh town, dark weathered wood on short stilts, reed-thatched roof, moss; 3: Abacus Heights, the hill town, golden sandstone, slate roof, arched doors; 4: The Crossroads, the farm town, red brick and timber, thatched roof.

1: The Assay Forge, the smelting town, black basalt blocks, copper roof, a tall chimney; 2: The Underledger, the cave town, carved grey cave stone, glowing blue crystal lanterns, a heavy door; 3: Windowspire, the mountain town, grey stone, steep snow-covered roof; 4: The Scriptorium, the marble city, white marble, columns, a bronze dome.

sections.name: Dojos, inside
sections.brief: The inside of an empty training hall, used as the floor of a game map. Seen from above and slightly in front, the same raised camera as a top-down role-playing game, so the floor fills most of the picture and the back wall shows as a band across the top. The back wall fills the top fifth of the image. Narrow side walls run down the left and right edges. A wide open doorway sits in the middle of the bottom edge. In the middle of the floor: the sparring ring described below. The rest of the floor is plain and even, with nothing standing on it: no people, no furniture, no weapons, no mats, no objects of any kind, because the game places those itself. Even daylight, hand-painted, bright and detailed, no text anywhere. {item}
items: This is the hall in Tallyport, the harbor town. Warm honey-colored wooden floorboards. Back wall of white plaster and dark timber beams, with tall windows looking out on the sea and blue-and-white cloth banners. The sparring ring is made of thick coiled rope laid on the floor, centered on the floor and taking up about half the width of the picture.

This is the hall in Sievemarsh, the marsh town. Dark weathered planks with reed mats along the edges. Back wall of dark wood with moss in the corners, reed blinds over the windows and green cloth banners. The sparring ring is made of woven reed matting edged with rope, centered on the floor and taking up about half the width of the picture.

This is the hall in Abacus Heights, the hill town. Smooth golden sandstone flagstones. Back wall of sandstone with arched windows and ochre cloth banners. The sparring ring is inlaid in darker stone, centered on the floor and taking up about half the width of the picture.

This is the hall in The Crossroads, the farm town. Broad pale oak floorboards. Back wall of red brick and timber with small square windows, hanging dried herbs and red cloth banners. The sparring ring is made of packed sawdust edged with a low wooden rail lying flat, centered on the floor and taking up about half the width of the picture.

This is the hall in The Assay Forge, the smelting town. Dark slate flagstones, warm with forge light. Back wall of black basalt with a glowing forge mouth set into it and copper-colored cloth banners. The sparring ring is made of iron plates riveted into the floor, centered on the floor and taking up about half the width of the picture.

This is the hall in The Underledger, the cave town. Smooth grey cave stone, cool and dim, lit by blue crystals set into the walls. Back wall of carved rock with glowing blue crystal lanterns and grey cloth banners. The sparring ring is made of glowing blue lines set into the stone, centered on the floor and taking up about half the width of the picture.

This is the hall in Windowspire, the mountain town. Pale scrubbed pine floorboards. Back wall of grey stone with frosted windows showing snowy peaks and white fur-trimmed banners. The sparring ring is made of red-painted boards, centered on the floor and taking up about half the width of the picture.

This is the hall in The Scriptorium, the marble city. Polished white marble with thin bronze inlay lines. Back wall of white marble columns with bronze lamps and deep blue cloth banners. The sparring ring is made of bronze set into the marble, centered on the floor and taking up about half the width of the picture.

sections.name: Running, five directions
sections.brief: A pixel-art sprite sheet of the person in the reference image: two rows of four cells, eight cells in all. The reference shows this same person; match their face, body, clothes, colors, size and pixel style exactly. In every one of the eight cells the person faces and moves the same way: {item} The eight cells are one smooth run cycle, in order left to right across the top row, then left to right across the bottom row. 1: right foot lands under the body, leaning forward. 2: right knee bends, body at its lowest. 3: right leg pushes off hard, left knee driving forward and up. 4: both feet off the ground, body at its highest, stride at its longest. 5 to 8: the same four poses with left and right swapped. The body leans forward and the arms pump hard, hands empty. The person is the same size in every cell, and nothing crosses from one cell into the next. The person is exactly the same height and scale in every cell. Pixel art in a realistic style: adult human proportions, about seven heads tall, with natural shoulders, hands and feet, not chibi and not cartoonish, like the hand-pixelled character sprites of classic late-1990s isometric role-playing games. The camera is raised, looking down at about thirty-five degrees. Soft light from the upper left. Clean, detailed, slightly muted natural colors. Cloth that can be dyed is drawn plain undyed off-white. Metal is drawn plain steel grey. Leather is natural brown. The game recolors the off-white and the grey, so keep them free of any other color. The head is completely bald and clean-shaven. The eyebrows stay; there is no other hair anywhere on the head, because the game adds hair separately. Nothing on the head, nothing in the hands. No ground, no shadow, nothing behind the person.
